answer: Random Wharf Assignment. Each epoch, a verifiable randomness beacon assigns every agent identity to one of N wharf slots; only one identity per slot can act, and beacon output is revealed only after registration closes. An attacker cannot precompute slot collisions, so k sybils collide with probability rising sharply with k, forcing excess identities into later velvet rounds with reduced weight. Registration requires a jade deposit refunded only if the slot is used, so each wasted sybil costs gas plus a locked deposit per epoch.
